Evening daily rules for airflow checks
This part of the manual describes the routine in plain words
Companion Animal Travel Desk routine for booking and care
The desk keeps companion travel steady from first contact to pickup, and the aim is to make each handoff calm, clear, and well noted. Staff should use the approved intake path for every booking, confirm the travel details with the traveler, and keep the record clean enough that another clerk can take over without guessing. <<FACT F085>> When a pet is accepted for travel, the file should show the animal's needs, the owner's contact details, and any handling notes that help the crew keep the trip smooth.

The desk also keeps an eye on comfort and safety through the full trip. Crates, carriers, and papers should be checked before release, and any concern about condition, behavior, or missing items should be written down in plain language. If the trip brings a delay, a gate change, or a problem at handoff, staff should stay calm, explain the next step in easy words, and avoid giving mixed messages. <<FACT F102>> The record should be updated as soon as the matter is known, with enough detail for the next person to pick up the thread without extra backtracking.

When travelers call back, staff should speak in a friendly way, keep the notes consistent, and make sure follow-up care is matched to the last known status of the pet. If a traveler such as Rina Chaudhary or Tomas Kaur checks on Toby, the answer should come from the file, not memory alone. For anything outside routine care, staff should pass the matter along at once and keep the handoff simple.

If anything is unclear, contact the senior coordinator or the duty supervisor right away.
